label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate with Moderate Screen Use
summary: This profile represents a psychologically resilient group characterized by notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With a UCLA-8 loneliness mean of 0.791, a PHQ-9 depression mean of 0.28, and a near-floor GAD-7 anxiety mean of 0.037, these respondents consistently score at the lowest end of all three distress measures. They are predominantly male, hold graduate-level or higher education, and report moderate daily screen or internet use of 1 to 3 hours.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores suggesting strong social connectedness
Near-zero anxiety levels on the GAD-7
Moderate and controlled daily screen or internet usage (1–3 hours)
High educational attainment suggesting structured daily routines and goal orientation

label: High-Distress Heavy-Use Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures respondents reporting elevated loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms relative to other clusters. Members score notably high on all three distress dimensions (UCLA-8 loneliness mean ≈ 1.66, PHQ-9 depression mean ≈ 1.65, GAD-7 anxiety mean ≈ 2.10), suggesting a co-occurring pattern of psychological burden. They are predominantly female, hold graduate-level or higher education, and report spending more than 5 hours daily on the activity measured. The cluster is moderately sized (n = 198), indicating this is not a fringe pattern but a substantial subgroup.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily usage exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.66) indicating persistent feelings of social disconnection
Moderately high depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 1.65) consistent with mild-to-moderate depression
Highest anxiety symptom levels among profiles (GAD-7 mean ≈ 2.10) suggesting frequent worry and tension
Heavy daily usage (more than 5 hours) potentially reflecting withdrawal, coping behavior, or compulsive engagement
Co-occurrence of all three distress indicators, pointing to a compounded psychological vulnerability
tone: Concerned and empathetic; the convergence of high loneliness, depression, and anxiety alongside heavy usage warrants careful, supportive interpretation

label: Resilient Well-Connected Graduate Woman
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. Across all three validated scales (UCLA-8, PHQ-9, GAD-7), mean scores fall well below clinical thresholds, indicating a generally positive psychological state with strong social connectedness and emotional stability.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/social-media use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.21, near the scale floor)
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.82, well below mild-depression cutoff)
Displays very low anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.79, well below clinical threshold)
Maintains moderate and bounded daily screen or social-media use (1–3 hours)
Holds advanced educational attainment, suggesting access to cognitive and social resources
tone: Calm, stable, and socially engaged — reflecting a respondent group that appears psychologically well-adjusted with low distress across all measured dimensions
